Add an analysis report to a supplement site

Source: R/add-report.R
add_report.Rd

add_report() writes a new report file, analyses/<name>.qmd, and adds a link to it as the last item of the Analyses menu in _quarto.yml. The home page of a site made from the template lists every report in analyses/ with its title and description, so the new report shows there too.

Usage

add_report(name, title, description = "", path = ".")

Arguments

name

The file name of the report, without .qmd. It is ASCII letters, digits, -, and _, and starts with a letter or a digit. It cannot be a name that Windows reserves for a device, in any letter case: CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1 to COM9, or LPT1 to LPT9.

title

The title of the report. It shows in the Analyses menu and on the home page.

description

A short description of the report for the home page. When it is "", the report has no description, and the home page shows the start of the report's text in its place.

path

The folder of the site.

Value

The path of the new report file, invisibly.

Details

The home page's table lists the reports that have an order field in their front matter first, by that number, and the others after them by title. The template's example report has order: 1. The function gives the new report the next whole number after the largest order of the other reports in analyses/. So when every report has an order and the menu lists them in that order, the table lists reports in the order of the Analyses menu. The new report gets order: 1 when analyses/ holds no other report. It gets no order when no other report has one, as in a site made before the template had order, so that its table keeps listing reports by title. Here an order counts only when the yaml package reads it as a number below one million (in absolute value), and a report whose front matter cannot be read counts as having none. To change the table's order, edit the order values, render each changed report by name, then render the whole site.

The first code chunk of the new report is the site chunk of the template's example report, which sets site to the site folder. If QUARTO_PROJECT_DIR is not empty, as in a render, site is its value. Otherwise site is "." or "..", the first of the two that holds _quarto.yml, and the chunk stops with an error if neither holds it. The chunk then reads _scripts/report.R with source(file.path(site, "_scripts", "report.R"), local = TRUE). That file defines save_png(), which saves a figure in figures/, and print_environment(). The report's text says to read a data file as file.path(site, "data", "<file name>").

A site made before the template had _scripts/report.R lacks the file. When the site has no _scripts/report.R, the function copies the template's file there, and it makes the _scripts folder when that is missing. It never replaces a _scripts/report.R that the site has. A report fails to render when that file lacks print_environment().

The new report ends with a "Computing environment" section, the same as the template's example report. It calls print_environment(), which prints the R and package versions of the render, with sessioninfo::session_info() when the sessioninfo package is installed and with utils::sessionInfo() otherwise. It shows the home folder as ~.

check_supplement() compares the text of each report with the hash in its stored output. If a report names _scripts/report.R and the file is missing, it gives a row. print_environment() also prints the MD5 of _scripts/report.R, and check_supplement() gives a row for each report whose stored output gives another MD5 than the file has now. After a change to the file, render each report by name to take the change.

The function adds lines to _quarto.yml as text, so the other lines of the file, its comments included, stay as they are. It finds the menu as the item with text: Analyses under website: navbar: left: (or right:), written in block style, with each item on its own line after a -. The title and the description are written as YAML strings in double quotes.

Quarto runs the new report the first time that the site renders, because it has no stored output in _freeze/ yet. To run it alone, render it by name, for example quarto render analyses/<name>.qmd.

Errors

The function writes nothing when it stops. Its own errors have the class supplement_error and one of these classes:

  • supplement_error_argument: path is not a single non-empty string, title is not a single string with a character other than white space, or description is not a single string.

  • supplement_error_report_name: name is not a single string of ASCII letters, digits, -, and _ that starts with a letter or a digit, or it is a name that Windows reserves for a device, in any letter case: CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1 to COM9, or LPT1 to LPT9.

  • supplement_error_line_break: title or description holds a line break.

  • supplement_error_no_config: path holds no _quarto.yml.

  • supplement_error_parse: the yaml package cannot read _quarto.yml. Examples are a [ or a { that is not closed, a key line indented with a tab, and a key given twice in one map. The message names the file and gives the message of the yaml package.

  • supplement_error_file_exists: the report file exists, or a file whose name differs from it only in letter case; analyses is not a folder or is a link; _scripts is not a folder or is a link; _scripts/report.R is a folder or a link; or _freeze/analyses/<name> exists, which holds the stored output of an earlier report of that name.

  • supplement_error_no_menu: _quarto.yml has no Analyses menu in block style. The error shows the lines to add by hand.

  • supplement_error_yaml: the yaml package does not read the changed _quarto.yml as the old menu with the new item added. The error shows the lines to add by hand.

  • supplement_error_encoding: title, description, or _quarto.yml is not UTF-8 text.

  • supplement_error_write: the analyses or _scripts folder could not be made, or a write failed after its file was opened, for example on a full disk. A _quarto.yml whose write failed gets its old text back.

When a file cannot be opened for writing, for example a read-only _quarto.yml, R's own error is shown. After any failed write, the function removes the report file, a _scripts/report.R that it copied, and any folder it made.

See also

add_data() to add a data file, and create_supplement() to make a site.

Examples

site <- file.path(tempdir(), "report-example")
create_supplement(site)
#> ✔ Made a supplement site in /tmp/RtmpCeDjpE/report-example.
#> ℹ Replace `OWNER/REPO` in _quarto.yml, and `OWNER` and `REPO` in the site
#>   address in _README.md, with your GitHub repository.
#> ℹ Put the paper facts in _supplement.yml.
#> ℹ Run `quarto render` in /tmp/RtmpCeDjpE/report-example, or
#>   `render_supplement()` in R with that folder as `path`, once before your first
#>   commit.
add_report("models", "Model Comparison", "Fits and compares the models.", path = site)
#> ✔ Wrote analyses/models.qmd and added it to the Analyses menu in _quarto.yml.
#> ℹ Run `quarto render analyses/models.qmd` in /tmp/RtmpCeDjpE/report-example, or
#>   `render_supplement("models")` in R in that folder, to run the report.
cat(readLines(file.path(site, "analyses", "models.qmd")), sep = "\n")
#> ---
#> title: "Model Comparison"
#> description: "Fits and compares the models."
#> order: 2
#> ---
#> 
#> Write the report here. The `site` chunk finds the site folder, so the
#> report reads a data file as `file.path(site, "data", "<file name>")`.
#> 
#> ```{r}
#> #| label: site
#> site <- Sys.getenv("QUARTO_PROJECT_DIR")
#> if (!nzchar(site)) {
#>   site <- Find(function(dir) file.exists(file.path(dir, "_quarto.yml")), c(".", ".."))
#> }
#> if (is.null(site)) {
#>   stop("Run this code from the site folder or from its analyses/ folder.")
#> }
#> source(file.path(site, "_scripts", "report.R"), local = TRUE)
#> ```
#> 
#> ```{r}
#> #| label: setup
#> set.seed(2026)
#> ```
#> 
#> ## Computing environment
#> 
#> This section shows the versions of R and of each package that the last render
#> of this report used, from `print_environment()` in `_scripts/report.R`. The
#> site stores this output with the rest, so the page keeps the versions that
#> made its results. Your home folder shows as `~`. Read the output before you
#> publish it, because a folder outside your home folder shows in full.
#> 
#> ::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="R and package versions"}
#> ```{r}
#> #| label: session-info
#> #| cache: false
#> print_environment()
#> ```
#> :::
unlink(site, recursive = TRUE)
